title: New results on the odd- and unique-Ramsey numbers
summary: The odd-Ramsey number $r_{\text{odd}}(n,H)$ of a graph $H$ is the minimum number of colors needed to edge-color $K_n$ so that in every copy of $H$ some color occurs an odd number of times, and the unique-Ramsey number $r_{\text{u}}(n,H)$ is the corresponding notion in which some color is required to occur not only an odd number of times but exactly once. In this paper, we address three questions from previous papers. We show $r_{\text{odd}}(n,K_{s,t})> n^{1/\left(\frac s2+\frac 1{2\lfloor t/8 \rfloor}\right)}$ when $s\leq t$ and $s$ is odd and $t$ is even, which is log-asymptotically tight…
